pattern_id: Causal Fork via Selective Ancestor Equivocation
description:
A Byzantine validator creates equivocating blocks at the same slot (round, author) with strategically different ancestor sets. By selectively broadcasting these blocks to different honest nodes, the Byzantine node causes honest nodes to build divergent DAG views. When each honest node independently commits and linearizes blocks based on their local DAG view, they produce different transaction orders, violating safety.

The attack works because:
1. Each equivocating block references a different subset of ancestors from the previous round
2. Honest nodes that receive different equivocating blocks build their subsequent blocks on top of different causal histories
3. The commit and linearization algorithms operate on each node's local DAG view independently
4. There is no mechanism to detect that different nodes have committed different equivocating blocks at the same slot
5. The protocol does not enforce convergence of linearized sequences across nodes

The vulnerability manifests when:
- Different honest nodes commit different equivocating blocks (B2_v1 vs B2_v2)
- The linearizer produces different transaction sequences on different nodes
- Nodes execute different state transitions, breaking consensus safety

To test for this pattern:
1. Create separate DagState instances for each honest node (to simulate independent views)
2. Create equivocating blocks with different ancestor sets at the same slot
3. Selectively add different equivocating blocks to different nodes' DAG states
4. Build subsequent rounds on each node based on their local view
5. Run commit and linearization on each node independently
6. Assert that all nodes produce identical linearized transaction sequences
7. Assert that if equivocation is detected, both blocks are excluded OR only one is committed across all nodes
trigger_condition: Byzantine validator creates equivocating blocks with different ancestor sets and selectively broadcasts them to partition the honest nodes' DAG views. Requires at least 3 honest nodes to observe divergence.
